hero.headline:
Gluten-free life,
told exactly as it is.
hero.body: Mother. Programmer. And for a few years now, an involuntary expert in reading labels. Here I talk about coeliac disease with no jargon and no sugar-coating — with just the right mix of useful and fed up that comes from asking "does this contain traces?" in every single restaurant.

about.title: From programmer to accidental advocate.
about.body: I was diagnosed with coeliac disease in 2018 and found out nobody explains what living with it is actually like: the packed lunch at every plan, the interrogation over every menu, and that feeling of being "the difficult one" in the group. I started posting about it on Instagram with humour because, if I don't laugh, nobody does.

meta.title: About me
meta.description: I'm Marta. Coeliac, mother and programmer, in that order depending on the day. Diagnosed in 2018, this is what I learned along the way.

hero.headline: I'm Marta. Coeliac, mother and programmer, in that order depending on the day.
hero.body: Diagnosed in 2018, overnight I went from eating whatever I fancied to reading labels like they were a new language. This is what I learned along the way — and what I'm still learning.

timeline.text: Coeliac diagnosis. The start of a crash course in "reading the small print on everything".
I start posting on Instagram what nobody talks about: the lunchbox in my backpack, the interrogation at every bar, and the funny side that's also in all of this.
@glutenfreemarta grows with reels, practical guides and a community that's just as fed up but laughs along with me. And now, with CeroGluten Lab, taking all of this one step further.

tone.title: Why the sarcastic tone?
tone.body: Because real coeliac disease isn't just "eating healthy". It's explaining for the hundredth time what a trace is, it's not being able to improvise a plan, it's sometimes feeling like the awkward one at the table. I'd rather laugh at that than let it define me. You won't find medical jargon here — that's what your doctor is for — but what living gluten-free is actually like.

meta.title: Cookies
meta.description: What cookies this site uses, what they are for and how to change your mind.

banner.label: Cookie notice
banner.body: I use measurement cookies to see which pages get read. They stay off unless you accept them.

page.headline: What cookies this site uses
page.intro: Just enough to remember your language and to see what gets read. No advertising, no profiling, no selling data.
page.necessaryBody: There is only one: it is called locale, it stores the language you pick in the switcher and it lasts a year. It is created only when you click, never before, so it needs no permission. Without it, the site would fall back to your browser's language on every visit.
page.analyticsBody: Google Tag Manager loads Google Analytics to count visits and see which pages are of interest. Its cookies start with _ga and can last up to two years. They do not load until you accept them, and if you reject them any earlier ones are deleted.
page.choiceAccepted: Right now you have accepted measurement cookies.
page.choiceRejected: Right now you have rejected measurement cookies.
page.choicePending: You have not chosen yet, so no measurement cookie is active.
page.choiceChange: You can change your mind whenever you like:
page.browserBody: On top of this, every browser lets you see and delete a site's cookies from its privacy settings.

audience.note: People who do the shopping, read labels and ask the group chat which bread does not taste like cardboard. If your product is gluten free, they are already looking for it.

formats.title: What I can do for your brand

items.title: Reel
items.body: What works best here: the product in a real situation, not on a set. If I would not eat it, I do not film it.

items.title: Carousel
items.body: For when there is something to actually explain: ingredients, certification, why that "gluten free" can be trusted.

items.title: Stories with a link
items.body: A series of stories with a direct link and a code if there is one. They stay in highlights instead of vanishing after 24 hours.

items.title: An honest review
items.body: I try the product and say how it went. If it is bad I will say so, and that is exactly why people believe me when it is good.
